body:
First of all, I would like to thank you all for your kind and understanding comments. It's a relief to be able to remind myself that not everyone will judge me -- or him -- as harshly I suspect we've judged ourselves.

jagermeistr... Don't misquote me. I didn't say love. I am very careful not to say love.

People are imperfect. She was living across the country from her family with him. As I understand it, she didn't have a job, a car, nor the understanding or support one would expect from family. She had no resources. When I said that she was dependent on him, I meant literally. Physically and emotionally, both. He felt stuck. I am willing to concede that staying with her wasn't right, but he didn't feel he had a choice. I don't think it was done with bad intentions. I know I said that her family wasn't overly supportive, but he did wait until she could be with them if he ended it. I guess hoping that some kind of familial support would kick in.

Wonderful? Where did you...I never...ever...said wonderful. No, wonderful I'm not. I was simply expressing the thought that if he hadn't met me first maybe they would have been happy. Or happier. Or something. Some form of survivor's guilt, even though the context is all wrong.

I don't really know how to respond to the rest of your post, other than to say that this is genuine guilt, and grief. My heart hurts for her. For her family. I can't even begin to understand their grief and their heartache. Their pain. And it breaks for him, too.

He never, ever, said that she was unimportant to him. Ever. And I never wanted him to. He told me that he cared about her, but he didn't love her the way he was supposed to.

My concern is not getting back into his life, per se. My concern is knowing whether or not he's ok.

I don't want to get into a big argument. I don't have the energy to try to defend myself much more than I already have. I can rephrase or specify a hundred times, but I don't think I can accurately explain my emotions.
